briefing:
Libreboot, bless their little hearts, decided their "anti-AI policy" was too much work after… *one month*. Amazing commitment to principles, truly. Guess those open-source purists realized that maybe AI isn't a demon to be banished but potentially a useful tool, or more likely, their contributor base dwindled faster than our hopes for stable deployments. The ideological pendulum swings faster than a dev lead changing requirements.

Speaking of stability, apparently GnuPG Made Easy – the irony writes itself – had a "critical security bug." Not just any bug, but one affecting *all existing releases* and basically *everything* that touches GPGME: email, XMPP, Flatpak, Samba. So, you know, just all your secure communications and software distribution pipelines, completely compromised. Announced late Friday afternoon, naturally, because nothing says "happy weekend" like realizing the digital equivalent of your front door lock was actually made of papier-mâché.

And finally, Intel's cooking up some Linux 7.5 magic to "better handle multiple GPUs with lots of VRAM." Read: the AI bubble needs more juice, and we finally figured out how to make two graphics cards play nice after only, what, three decades of trying? This isn't for *us*, it's for the folks training another generative AI model to tell us what a cat looks like, but with more steps and significantly higher energy consumption. Just pump more hardware at the problem, that'll fix everything.

evidence.title: Libreboot Abandons Anti-AI Policy After One Month
GnuPG's GPGME Affected By Critical Security Bug In Turn Affecting Mail Clients, Flatpak
evidence.facts:
• Werner Koch announced a late Friday afternoon "critical security bug" affecting GnuPG's GPGME library - GnuPG Made Easy.
• Unfortunately this in turn affects GPGME users like most email clients, most XMPP clients, Flatpak, Samba, and other software.
• This critical security bug made public today affects all existing releases of GnuPG Made Easy.

evidence.title: Intel Preps Linux 7.5 Change To Better Handle Multiple GPUs With Lots Of VRAM
